message:
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
`module.secure_baseline.module.analyzer_baseline_eu-central-1:resource.aws_accessanalyzer_analyzer.default` is created with `type = "ORGANIZATION"` (`is_organization = local.is_master_account`), which requires the organization and the `access-analyzer.amazonaws.com` service access enabled by `:resource.aws_organizations_organization.org`. It has no dependency on that resource; the official provider documentation for this resource type shows `depends_on = [aws_organizations_organization.example]` as the required pattern for ORGANIZATION-type analyzers.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
The analyzer in module.secure_baseline.module.analyzer_baseline_eu-central-1 is created with type "ORGANIZATION" (is_organization=true), which requires the AWS Organizations organization to already exist. No attribute reference or depends_on connects this analyzer to the organization resource, so Terraform may provision the analyzer before :resource.aws_organizations_organization.org, causing an API failure or a wrong-scope analyzer. Add depends_on = [aws_organizations_organization.org] to the analyzer resource (or to the module call).

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:resource.google_folder_iam_member.bindings sets `folder` from `local.folder.name`, which resolves to :resource.google_folder.folder when var.folder_create is true. No dependency is expressed, so this additive IAM member could be applied before the folder exists.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
google_folder_iam_member.bindings sets folder = local.folder.name, which resolves to google_folder.folder[0] when folder_create is true, but no dependency on the folder resource is recorded. Additive bindings could be applied before the folder exists. Remedy: depends_on = [google_folder.folder].

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
google_folder_iam_member.bindings applies additive IAM members with folder = local.folder.name, but the graph shows no dependency on the folder resource. The member binding cannot be created before the folder exists; the dependency is only expressed via the local.folder local.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
`google_project_iam_member.shared_vpc_host_robots` grants roles on the host project to this project's service-agent robot accounts (e.g. `service-NUMBER@gcp-sa-*`), constructed from `local.service_accounts_robots` / `local.service_account_cloud_services`. Those robot service identities only come into existence once the corresponding APIs are enabled in this project — exactly the ordering that the parallel resource `google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member.service_identity_cmek` enforces via its explicit `depends_on` on `google_project_service.project_services`. `shared_vpc_host_robots` has no such dependency, so the grants may be created before the identities they target exist.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
`google_project_iam_member.shared_vpc_host_robots` grants roles in the host project to this project's service robot identities (e.g. `service-<num>@gcp-sa-*`, `service_account_cloud_services`). These robot service accounts are only created when their corresponding APIs are enabled in this project, but the resource has no dependency on `google_project_service.project_services`, so the IAM grant can race API activation and fail with a nonexistent-serviceAccount error.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
google_project_iam_member.shared_vpc_host_robots grants roles in the host project to this project's Google-managed robot service identities (e.g. service-NUMBER@gcp-sa-*). These service accounts are only created after the corresponding APIs are enabled, i.e. after google_project_service.project_services completes (SA creation is asynchronous following API activation). Without this dependency Terraform may attempt the IAM grant before the robot service account exists and the API will reject the unknown member. The module already expresses this ordering for every other consumer of these identities (see google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member.service_identity_cmek and the service_accounts output), but this resource has none.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
The AWS Config recorder started by module.config_baseline_us-west-2 (aws_config_configuration_recorder_status.recorder) uses a delivery channel whose s3_bucket_name is passed in as a plain string, so there is no dependency on the audit-log bucket policy. Starting the configuration recorder requires the S3 bucket policy to permit config.amazonaws.com delivery; if :resource.aws_s3_bucket_policy.audit_log is applied after this module, StartConfigurationRecorder fails with InsufficientDeliveryPolicyException. The bucket policy must be in place before the recorder is started.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
module.config_baseline_us-west-2 creates an aws_config_delivery_channel pointing at the audit log bucket (via s3_bucket_name). AWS Config validates that the bucket policy grants config.amazonaws.com write access when the delivery channel is created (InsufficientDeliveryPolicyException), but the module has no dependency on resource.aws_s3_bucket_policy.audit_log. Add a depends_on on the audit log bucket policy.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
data.template_file.runners renders the runner config with vars.bucket_name sourced from local.bucket_name, which resolves to module.cache.bucket when cache_bucket.create is true. The rendered config (which ends up in the runner agent's user-data) references the cache bucket, so the data source should depend on the cache module being created; no such dependency is expressed.

data.template_file.runners renders the runner config.toml with the S3 cache bucket name taken from local.bucket_name, which resolves to module.cache.bucket, but the graph shows no dependency on module.runner:module.cache. The cache bucket must exist (and its name be known) before the runner configuration referencing it is rendered and baked into the runner agent's user data. Inlining the local's expression as a direct reference to module.cache establishes the ordering as a data dependency.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
The null_resource register_aks_msi_preview_feature runs a local-exec script that registers the Microsoft.ContainerService "AAD-V2" feature and polls until the provider reports it as Registered (the source notes this can take around 30 minutes). The AKS cluster is created with managed Azure AD RBAC (role_based_access_control.azure_active_directory.managed = true), which requires that feature/preview registration to be complete before the cluster can be provisioned. However, azurerm_kubernetes_cluster.aks references none of the null_resource's outputs (it has none) and no attribute reference or depends_on orders the cluster after the registration resource, so Terraform may create the cluster before (or concurrently with) feature registration and fail. Add an explicit depends_on from the cluster to the null_resource.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
module.aks_clusters:resource.azurerm_kubernetes_cluster.aks configures role_based_access_control with azure_active_directory managed = true unconditionally, which requires the Microsoft.ContainerService AAD-V2 preview feature and provider to be registered first. module.aks_clusters:resource.null_resource.register_aks_msi_preview_feature performs exactly that registration via local-exec (and can take ~30 minutes), but the cluster has no dependency on it — nothing references the null_resource, so Terraform may create the cluster before (or without waiting for) the feature registration, failing cluster creation. A bare depends_on is required; no attribute of the cluster can carry this ordering.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
The AKS cluster module.aks_clusters:resource.azurerm_kubernetes_cluster.aks enables managed Azure AD (role_based_access_control.azure_active_directory.managed = true), which requires the AAD-V2 preview feature to be registered with Microsoft.ContainerService. The null_resource register_aks_msi_preview_feature performs that registration (and can take ~30 minutes to complete), but the cluster has no dependency on it, so the cluster can be created before the feature registration finishes and fail. Add `depends_on = [null_resource.register_aks_msi_preview_feature]` to the cluster.

IAM bindings could be applied before the folder exists, failing the apply. Remedy: depends_on = [google_folder.folder].

The binding cannot be created before google_folder.folder exists; the ordering is only mediated through the local.folder local (try(google_folder.folder.0, ...)), which the mechanical analysis cannot trace.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
The CloudTrail trail created by module.cloudtrail_baseline (aws_cloudtrail.global) receives the audit-log bucket name as a plain string, so Terraform infers no dependency on the bucket policy. CloudTrail's CreateTrail API validates that the S3 bucket policy permits cloudtrail.amazonaws.com; if :resource.aws_s3_bucket_policy.audit_log has not been applied yet, trail creation fails with InsufficientS3BucketPolicyException. The aws_s3_bucket_policy should be created before the trail is created (the provider's own documentation shows a bare `depends_on` on the bucket policy for exactly this race).

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
module.cloudtrail_baseline creates the aws_cloudtrail trail, which validates the S3 bucket policy at creation time (AWS returns InsufficientS3BucketPolicyException if the policy granting cloudtrail.amazonaws.com access isn't applied yet). It only receives local.audit_log_bucket_id (the bucket id), so nothing orders it after resource.aws_s3_bucket_policy.audit_log. Add a depends_on on the audit log bucket policy.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
The EKS managed node group is created without any ordering relative to its node IAM role policy attachments. EKS validates node role permissions when provisioning the node group, and IAM policy changes propagate asynchronously: without the AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy/AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy/AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly policies attached and propagated before node group creation, launched nodes cannot join the cluster, and node group deletion may fail to clean up EC2 instances and ENIs. The launch template has a bare `depends_on` on the base attachment, but the node group resource itself has no dependency on either attachment.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
aws_eks_node_group.this provision instances asynchronously and can launch/join the cluster before aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this is applied. The node role (aws_iam_role.this) must have its policies attached first (AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy, AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy, AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly), otherwise nodes join without permissions and EKS cannot properly manage EC2 instances and ENIs.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:resource.aws_lambda_function.dispatcher is wired to EventBridge (rule/target) and starts receiving workflow_job events as soon as they are published, but its CloudWatch log group :resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.dispatcher is only created after the function (via the `name = "/aws/lambda/${aws_lambda_function.dispatcher.function_name}"` reference). An invocation before the log group exists makes Lambda auto-create it with default settings, losing the configured retention_in_days/kms_key_id/log_group_class and failing the apply with ResourceAlreadyExistsException. The log group must exist before the function: compute the log group name from var.config.prefix instead of function_name, and add a dependency from the function to the log group (e.g. logging_config.log_group = aws_cloudwatch_log_group.dispatcher.name, or a bare depends_on once the name reference is removed to avoid a cycle).

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
aws_lambda_function.dispatcher should be created after aws_cloudwatch_log_group.dispatcher: the log group defines retention/KMS/class settings for the function's /aws/lambda/${function_name} group, and if Lambda is invoked before it exists, Lambda auto-creates the default log group, defeating those settings and causing ResourceAlreadyExists errors on later applies. Note the dependency currently points the wrong way (the log group's name references the function's function_name, and a plain depends_on would form a cycle) — the log group name should be decoupled (e.g. "/aws/lambda/${var.config.prefix}-dispatch-to-runner", matching the function name) so the function can wait on the log group.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
aws_lambda_function.dispatcher is created before aws_cloudwatch_log_group.dispatcher (the log group's name references the function, inverting the required order). If the function is invoked (e.g. by the EventBridge target) before the log group resource is created, Lambda auto-creates a default log group and the aws_cloudwatch_log_group creation then fails with ResourceAlreadyExistsException. The log group must exist before the function can be invoked; note that a bare depends_on would cycle with the current name reference, so the log group name should be derived from var.config.prefix (e.g. "/aws/lambda/${var.config.prefix}-dispatch-to-runner") and the lambda given an explicit depends_on on the log group.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:resource.google_monitoring_notification_channel.channels uses the Cloud Monitoring API (via `project = local.project.project_id`), but the graph shows no dependency (implicit or explicit) on :resource.google_project_service.project_services. Monitoring is not enabled by default on new projects; if this module is enabling `monitoring.googleapis.com` in the same apply, channel creation can run before the API is active and fail. The module already uses an explicit depends_on on project_services for every other API-dependent resource (e.g. google_compute_project_metadata_item.default, google_logging_project_sink.sink, google_cloud_quotas_quota_preference.default); this resource is missing it.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
:resource.google_monitoring_notification_channel.channels calls the Cloud Monitoring API against `local.project.project_id`, but has no ordering relationship with :resource.google_project_service.project_services. Sibling observability resources in this module (e.g. logging sinks, quota preferences) already depend on project_services for exactly this reason; without it, channels can be applied before monitoring.googleapis.com is activated and fail with an API-not-enabled error.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
:resource.google_monitoring_notification_channel.channels creates notification channels via the Cloud Monitoring API, which is not enabled by default; if monitoring.googleapis.com is being activated by :resource.google_project_service.project_services in the same apply, channel creation races the API activation and fails. Every other API-dependent resource in this module (quotas, compute metadata, sinks, service identities) declares depends_on on :resource.google_project_service.project_services, but this one does not.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:resource.aws_eks_addon.adot references :resource.aws_iam_role.adot_collector via service_account_role_arn but not its policy attachments; if :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.adot_collector applies after the addon, the ADOT collector cannot write to Prometheus/X-Ray/CloudWatch.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
aws_eks_addon.adot sets service_account_role_arn from aws_iam_role.adot_collector.arn but does not depend on aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.adot_collector. The addon provider docs require the service-account role to already have the IAM permissions the addon needs; if the addon is applied before the Prometheus/X-Ray/CloudWatch policy attachments, the collector pods fail authorization.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
`null_resource.delete_daemonset` removes the `aws-node` daemonset (disabling the AWS VPC CNI), while `null_resource.create_calico_installation` applies the Calico Installation that takes over pod networking. Both resources depend only on `null_resource.update_kubeconfig`, so Terraform may delete `aws-node` before Calico's Installation exists, leaving pods without pod networking. Calico's standard EKS install order requires deleting `aws-node` only after the Installation is applied. Since both are local-exec kubectl resources, no attribute reference can express this ordering.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
null_resource.delete_daemonset runs 'kubectl delete daemonset -n kube-system aws-node' as part of the Calico CNI migration, but it has no dependency on null_resource.create_calico_installation. Nothing in the graph orders the aws-node daemonset deletion after the Calico Installation resource is created; in a single apply these two null_resources can run concurrently, and removing aws-node before Calico is installed can break pod networking. It should depend on null_resource.create_calico_installation (bare depends_on; no data-reference fix is possible for these null_resources).

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
google_compute_organization_security_policy_association.attachment attaches firewall policies by ID taken only from var.firewall_policy_attachments, with no reference to the policies created in this module. Since association creation calls the addAssociation API against the policy, each policy in google_compute_organization_security_policy.policy must exist before its association is created; without an explicit depends_on the associations may be applied before the policies, causing API errors on create and premature deletion ordering on destroy.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
google_compute_organization_security_policy_association.attachment sets policy_id from var.firewall_policy_attachments with no reference to the policies created by this module. When the attached policy is one created by google_compute_organization_security_policy.policy (the module's own firewall_policy_id output exists precisely for this), the association can be applied before the policy exists, and the organizationSecurityPolicies.addAssociation API call will fail. The association must be ordered after the policy resource.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
google_compute_organization_security_policy_association.attachment attaches hierarchical firewall policies whose IDs are supplied via var.firewall_policy_attachments, but the module itself creates those policies as google_compute_organization_security_policy.policy. Because the association references only the variable, Terraform may create the association before (or concurrently with) the policy, and the GCP addAssociation API will fail with 'policy not found' on a fresh apply. An explicit depends_on on the policy resource is needed to enforce the real-world creation order.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
For the just-in-time services (`secretmanager`, `pubsub`, `cloudasset`), the robot service account referenced by `google_project_iam_member.shared_vpc_host_robots` is only created when `google_project_service_identity.jit_si` runs (it does not appear merely from API activation). If `shared_vpc_service_config.service_identity_iam` targets one of these services, the IAM grant can be applied before the service identity exists; `google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member.service_identity_cmek` handles this with an explicit `depends_on` on `jit_si`, and `shared_vpc_host_robots` should as well.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
When service_identity_iam is configured for a just-in-time service (secretmanager, pubsub, cloudasset), the referenced member is the service identity that google_project_service_identity.jit_si explicitly triggers into existence; that generation is an asynchronous operation (create timeout of 20 minutes) and the service account does not exist until it succeeds. google_project_iam_member.shared_vpc_host_robots references these identities but has no dependency on jit_si, so the IAM grant can race ahead of identity creation and fail with an unknown member error.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:resource.google_monitoring_monitored_project.primary registers this project in metrics scopes through the Cloud Monitoring API, but the graph shows no dependency on :resource.google_project_service.project_services. The monitoring API is not enabled by default, so when this module provisions `monitoring.googleapis.com` in the same apply the monitored-project registration may execute before the API is usable. Like the other API-dependent resources in this module, it needs an explicit ordering on :resource.google_project_service.project_services.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
:resource.google_monitoring_monitored_project.primary uses the Cloud Monitoring API but has no dependency on :resource.google_project_service.project_services; the monitoring API must be activated in the project before monitored projects can be registered.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
:resource.google_monitoring_monitored_project.primary registers this project under a metrics scope using the Monitoring API (locations.global.metricsScopes.projects), which requires monitoring.googleapis.com to be enabled in this project. The API activation is performed by :resource.google_project_service.project_services, but this resource does not depend on it, so the two can race on a fresh project.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
delete_http_listener depends on set_frontend_port (create-time) instead of delete_frontend_port. The listener's PORT references var.settings.frontend_ports[...] (or the gateway's frontend port of the same name), so the listener must be deleted from the Application Gateway before the frontend port. delete_frontend_port has no depends_on at all, so its destroy-time provisioner may run in any order relative to the listener deletion; since the listener delete uses on_failure = fail, deleting the port first can fail the destroy. Add depends_on = [null_resource.delete_frontend_port, ...] to delete_http_listener.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
resource.null_resource.delete_http_listener has a destroy-time provisioner that deletes HTTP listeners which reference frontend ports, but it does not depend on null_resource.delete_frontend_port. Its depends_on list references null_resource.set_frontend_port instead (almost certainly a typo for the delete counterpart), so on destroy the frontend port can be deleted while a listener still references it, failing the Application Gateway update (and the provisioner uses on_failure = fail). Adding depends_on on delete_frontend_port ensures listeners are removed before the frontend port.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
null_resource.delete_http_listener deletes listeners that reference frontend ports (PORT = try(var.settings.frontend_ports[each.value.front_end_port_key].name, ...)), so the frontend port must be deleted after the listener on destroy. The resource's explicit depends_on includes null_resource.set_frontend_port (keeping the set-resource alive past the listener delete) but not null_resource.delete_frontend_port, the resource that actually performs the deletion; delete_frontend_port has no depends_on and no dependents, so its delete script can race with or precede the listener deletion (delete_http_listener has on_failure = fail). delete_http_listener should also depend_on null_resource.delete_frontend_port.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:resource.aws_launch_template.gitlab_runner_instance sets `iam_instance_profile.name = local.aws_iam_role_instance_name` (a plain string), so Terraform infers no dependency on :resource.aws_iam_instance_profile.instance. The launch template (and the ASG that consumes it) can be created before the instance profile exists, which makes launching the runner agent fail. A bare depends_on (guarded by var.create_runner_iam_role) is needed here.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
:resource.aws_launch_template.gitlab_runner_instance sets iam_instance_profile.name from local.aws_iam_role_instance_name (a name string), so Terraform orders it independently of :resource.aws_iam_instance_profile.instance. EC2 validates the instance profile when the launch template is created/updated, so the profile must exist first; the two can currently be applied in the wrong order.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
:resource.aws_launch_template.gitlab_runner_instance sets `iam_instance_profile.name` to the plain string `local.aws_iam_role_instance_name`, establishing no dependency on :resource.aws_iam_instance_profile.instance. On a fresh apply the ASG can launch instances before the instance profile exists, and instance launches will fail until the profile is created.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
aws_cloudwatch_log_group.ami_housekeeper currently depends on aws_lambda_function.ami_housekeeper (its name references aws_lambda_function.ami_housekeeper.function_name), so the function is created first and the managed log group afterwards. If the function is invoked in that window (it is wired to a scheduled EventBridge rule), Lambda auto-creates /aws/lambda/<name> with default settings, which then collides with this resource ("The specified log group already exists"). The documented pattern is to pre-create the log group and add a bare depends_on on the function. Note: adding that depends_on requires first decoupling the log group's name from the function — e.g. name = "/aws/lambda/${var.prefix}-ami-housekeeper", which matches function_name = "${var.prefix}-ami-housekeeper" — otherwise a cycle would result.

Nodes launched from this template use the instance profile credentials, so pods requiring permissions granted by the additional policies can start before those attachments take effect, causing AccessDenied failures on create/destroy.
